prov.text: We maintain the allowance at a level that we deem appropriate to adequately cover the expected credit losses in the loan and lease portfolio. Our provision for credit losses for loans and leases for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $6.1 million compared to $2.9 million in the same period of 2025, an increase of $3.2 million. As of September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, our allowance for credit losses was $45.6 million and $40.9 million, respectively, which we deemed to be adequate at each of the respective dates. Our allowance for credit loss as a percentage of total loans and leases was 0.94% at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively. During the quarter ending March 31, 2026, the Bank enhanced its ACL methodology for loans and leases. See Note 1. Recently Modified Accounting Policies and Allowance for Credit Losses in the Notes to our Consolidated Financial Statements in this Form 10-Q for further information related to these changes.

tax.text: 1 Yields related to tax-exempt loans exempt from income taxes are stated on a taxable-equivalent basis assuming a federal income tax rate of 21.0%. The taxable-equivalent adjustment was $157 thousand and $244 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively.

net.text: Net income was $18.6 million, or $1.10 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $13.7 million, or $0.81 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2025. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, when compared to the comparable period in 2025, the increase in net income of $4.9 million was due to an increase in net interest income after provision for credit losses of $6.5 million, offset by a decrease in noninterest income of $506 thousand, an increase in noninterest expense of $2.5 million and a decrease in income tax expense of $1.4 million. The tax equivalent net interest margin was 3.45% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.25% for the third quarter of 2025. Noninterest income to average assets was 0.52% for the third quarter of 2026, decreasing from 0.61% for the third quarter of 2025. Noninterest expense to average assets decreased to 2.34% in the third quarter of 2026, from 2.38% in the third quarter of 2025.

Net interest income.text: Net interest income, taxable equivalent, increased to $49.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, up from $42.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. Net interest income increased due to higher loan and lease balances and lower cost of interest-bearing liabilities. Average interest-earning assets increased from $5.23 billion for the third quarter of 2025, to $5.71 billion for the third quarter of 2026, primarily from the increase in our average loan and lease balances and average securities balances, which was offset by decreases in cash balances. Over this period, average loan and lease balances increased by $604.5 million and average interest-bearing deposits increased by $447.1 million. Average securities increased by $55.2 million, average federal funds sold and other interest earning assets decreased by $175.4 million, average subordinated debt increased by $13.7 million, average borrowings decreased by $4.0 million and noninterest-bearing deposits increased by $1.8 million. The tax equivalent net interest margin increased to 3.45% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.25% for the third quarter of 2025. The yield on earning assets increased from 5.68% for the third quarter of 2025, to 5.72% for the third quarter of 2026, primarily due to the deployment of excess cash and cash equivalents into loans and leases.

intro.text: SmartFinancial, Inc. (“SmartFinancial” or the “Company”) was incorporated on September 19, 1983, under the laws of the State of Tennessee. SmartFinancial is a bank holding company registered under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. In this Report on Form 10-K, the words “SmartFinancial,” “the Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to SmartFinancial, Inc. together with SmartBank and SmartBank’s wholly-owned subsidiaries, except where the context requires otherwise. The Company makes our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act available free of charge on our website at www.smartbank.com as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file such material with the SEC.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
